questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक देश दक्षेस (सार्क) का सदस्य नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries is not a member of SAARC ?
questions.solution: China (option B) is not a member of SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation). SAARC has eight member states: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Afghanistan. China is a much larger East Asian nation and geographically does not fall within South Asia. Nepal, Maldives, and Sri Lanka are all founding or original members of SAARC, making option B the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: चीन (विकल्प B) दक्षेस (दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्रीय सहयोग संगठन) का सदस्य नहीं है। दक्षेस के आठ सदस्य देश हैं: भारत, पाकिस्तान, बांग्लादेश, नेपाल, भूटान, श्रीलंका, मालदीव और अफगानिस्तान। चीन पूर्वी एशिया का देश है और भौगोलिक दृष्टि से दक्षिण एशिया में नहीं आता।
questions.chapter: South Asia and the Contemporary World

questions.text: मालदीव में बहुदलीय व्यवस्था को किस वर्ष शुरू किया गया ?
questions.text_english: In which year was a multi-party system introduced in the Maldives ?
questions.solution: A multi-party system was introduced in the Maldives in 2008 (option A). The Maldives had been under the authoritarian rule of President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom for thirty years. In 2008, a new democratic constitution was adopted and the first multiparty presidential elections were held, which Gayoom lost to Mohamed Nasheed. The other years — 2005, 2006, and 2007 — saw earlier steps toward political reform, but the formal introduction of the multiparty system and the first elections under it occurred in 2008.
questions.solution_hindi: मालदीव में बहुदलीय व्यवस्था 2008 में शुरू की गई (विकल्प A)। 2008 में नया लोकतांत्रिक संविधान अपनाया गया और पहला बहुदलीय राष्ट्रपति चुनाव हुआ।

questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र का कौन-सा एक अंग वर्तमान में स्थगित है ?
questions.text_english: Which one organ of the United Nations stands suspended at present ?
questions.solution: The Trusteeship Council (option C) is the organ of the United Nations that stands suspended at present. It was established to oversee the administration of trust territories and ensure their progress toward self-governance. By 1994, all trust territories had attained independence or self-governance, so the Council formally suspended its operations on 1 November 1994. The Secretariat, Economic and Social Council, and International Court of Justice continue to function actively.
questions.solution_hindi: न्यासिता परिषद (विकल्प C) संयुक्त राष्ट्र का वह अंग है जो वर्तमान में स्थगित है। 1994 तक सभी न्यास क्षेत्र स्वतंत्र हो गए, इसलिए परिषद ने 1 नवम्बर 1994 से अपना कार्य स्थगित कर दिया।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए : (i) विश्व बैंक की स्थापना (ii) संयुक्त राष्ट्र का गठन (iii) विश्व व्यापार संगठन की स्थापना (iv) अन्तर्राष्ट्रीय परमाणु ऊर्जा एजेन्सी की स्थापना
questions.text_english: Arrange the following in chronological order : (i) Creation of the World Bank (ii) Foundation of the United Nations (iii) World Trade Organisation was set up (iv) Establishment of the International Atomic Energy Agency
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is option B: (i), (ii), (iv), (iii). The World Bank was created in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference. The United Nations was founded in 1945. The International Atomic Energy Agency was established in 1957. The World Trade Organisation was set up in 1995. Thus the correct sequence is World Bank (1944) → United Nations (1945) → IAEA (1957) → WTO (1995), which corresponds to option B.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम विकल्प B है: (i), (ii), (iv), (iii)। विश्व बैंक 1944 में, संयुक्त राष्ट्र 1945 में, IAEA 1957 में और WTO 1995 में स्थापित हुआ।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : भारत ने अगस्त 2002 में क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल का अनुमोदन किया और उस पर हस्ताक्षर किए। कारण (R) : भारत पर्यावरण संरक्षण के वैश्विक प्रयासों में शामिल होने के लिए इच्छुक नहीं था।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : India signed and ratified the Kyoto Protocol in August 2002. Reason (R) : India was reluctant to participate in global efforts of environment conservation.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R). Choose the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. The Assertion is factually correct — India did sign and ratify the Kyoto Protocol in August 2002. However, the Reason is false because India was not reluctant to participate in global environmental efforts; on the contrary, India has consistently supported international environmental cooperation. India ratified the Protocol willingly, though as a developing country it was not required to make binding emission cuts under its terms. Since the Assertion is correct but the Reason incorrectly explains India's motivation, option C is the right choice.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है। अभिकथन सत्य है क्योंकि भारत ने अगस्त 2002 में क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल का अनुमोदन किया था। कारण असत्य है क्योंकि भारत पर्यावरण संरक्षण के प्रयासों में अनिच्छुक नहीं था; बल्कि भारत ने स्वेच्छा से प्रोटोकॉल को अनुमोदित किया।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा के बारे में सत्य है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is true about Global Commons ?

options.A: वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा का निर्धारण संयुक्त राष्ट्र करता है।
options.B: वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा किसी एक राज्य (देश) के क्षेत्राधिकार से परे होती है।
options.C: वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा का निर्धारण क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल ने किया है।
options.D: वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा का स्वामित्व बड़े देशों के पास है।

options_english.A: Global Commons are determined by the United Nations.
options_english.B: Global Commons are outside the sovereign jurisdiction of any one state.
options_english.C: Global Commons have been determined by the Kyoto Protocol.
options_english.D: Global Commons are owned by big powers.

questions.solution: Option B is the correct statement about Global Commons. Global Commons are areas or resources that lie outside the sovereign jurisdiction of any single state and belong to all of humanity collectively. Examples include the high seas, outer space, the Antarctic, and the atmosphere. They are not determined by the United Nations (A is wrong), not defined by the Kyoto Protocol (C is wrong), and certainly not owned by big powers (D is wrong). The defining characteristic of Global Commons is precisely that no state can exercise exclusive sovereignty over them.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा वे क्षेत्र या संसाधन हैं जो किसी एक देश के क्षेत्राधिकार से परे हैं और संपूर्ण मानवता की साझी संपत्ति हैं, जैसे उच्च समुद्र, बाह्य अंतरिक्ष, अंटार्कटिका और वायुमंडल।

questions.text: कॉलम 'A' में दिए गए नेताओं के नामों का कॉलम 'B' में दर्ज तथ्यों से सही मिलान कीजिए। कॉलम A: 1. सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल, 2. बोधचन्द्र सिंह, 3. पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु, 4. जवाहरलाल नेहरू। कॉलम B: (i) ट्रिस्ट विद डेस्टिनी, (ii) प्रथम उप-प्रधानमंत्री, (iii) विशाल-आन्ध्र आन्दोलन, (iv) एक देशी रियासत के राजा।
questions.text_english: Match the Leaders in the Column 'A' with the Facts listed in the Column 'B' correctly. Column A: 1. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, 2. Bodhchandra Singh, 3. Potti Sriramulu, 4. Jawaharlal Nehru. Column B: (i) Tryst with Destiny, (ii) First Deputy Prime Minister, (iii) Vishalandhra Movement, (iv) Maharaja of a Princely State.
questions.solution: The correct matching is option B: 1-(ii), 2-(iv), 3-(iii), 4-(i). Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was India's first Deputy Prime Minister (ii). Bodhchandra Singh was the Maharaja of Manipur, a princely state (iv). Potti Sriramulu led the Vishalandhra Movement demanding a separate Telugu-speaking state, and died after a prolonged fast in 1952, which eventually led to the creation of Andhra Pradesh (iii). Jawaharlal Nehru delivered the famous 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on the eve of India's independence (i).
questions.solution_hindi: सही मिलान विकल्प B है: 1-(ii) सरदार पटेल प्रथम उप-प्रधानमंत्री थे; 2-(iv) बोधचन्द्र सिंह मणिपुर रियासत के महाराजा थे; 3-(iii) पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु ने विशाल-आन्ध्र आन्दोलन का नेतृत्व किया; 4-(i) नेहरू ने 'ट्रिस्ट विद डेस्टिनी' भाषण दिया।
questions.topic: Integration of Princely States and State Reorganisation

questions.text: कथन I : औपनिवेशिक काल में राज्यों (प्रांतों) की सीमाओं का प्रशासनिक सुविधा के आधार पर सीमांकन किया गया था। कथन II : स्वतंत्रता के बाद प्रांतीय सीमाओं का पुनः निर्धारण भिन्न भाषाओं पर आधारित था।
questions.text_english: Statement I : During colonial period, the state boundaries were drawn on the administrative convenience. Statement II : After independence, redrawing of the boundaries of the states was based on different languages.
questions.instruction_line: उपर्युक्त दिए गए कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: In the light of the above given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।
options.C: कथन I सही है, परंतु कथन II गलत है।
options.D: कथन I गलत है, परंतु कथन II सही है।

options_english.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options_english.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
options_english.C: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options_english.D: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true. During the colonial period, the British drew state (provincial) boundaries purely for administrative convenience, without regard for linguistic or cultural identities. After independence, under popular demand, the States Reorganisation Commission (1953) recommended reorganising states on linguistic lines. This led to the creation of Andhra Pradesh in 1953 (the first linguistically formed state) and the broader reorganisation of states in 1956 on the basis of language. Both statements are therefore historically accurate.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। दोनों कथन सही हैं। औपनिवेशिक काल में सीमाएं प्रशासनिक सुविधा के आधार पर बनाई गईं थीं। स्वतंत्रता के बाद 1956 में राज्य पुनर्गठन आयोग की सिफारिश पर भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों की सीमाओं का पुनर्निर्धारण किया गया।

questions.text: 1957 में किस राज्य में कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया के नेतृत्व में एक मिली-जुली सरकार बनी थी ?
questions.text_english: In which state was a coalition government formed in 1957 under the leadership of Communist Party of India ?
questions.solution: In 1957, Kerala (option B) became the first state in the world where a Communist Party came to power through democratic elections. The Communist Party of India, led by E.M.S. Namboodiripad, formed a government in Kerala after winning the state assembly elections. This was a landmark moment in Indian politics, demonstrating that communist parties could participate in and win democratic elections. West Bengal, Assam, and Andhra Pradesh did not have CPI-led governments in 1957.
questions.solution_hindi: 1957 में केरल (विकल्प B) में कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया के नेतृत्व में ई.एम.एस. नम्बूदिरिपाद की सरकार बनी। यह विश्व का पहला उदाहरण था जब किसी कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ने लोकतांत्रिक चुनाव जीतकर सरकार बनाई।
questions.topic: Communist Party of India and State Politics

questions.text: रफी अहमद किदवई का संबंध किस राजनीतिक पार्टी से था ?
questions.text_english: To which political party did Rafi Ahmed Kidwai belong ?
questions.solution: Rafi Ahmed Kidwai belonged to the Indian National Congress (option B). He was a close associate of Jawaharlal Nehru and served as the Minister of Food and Agriculture in independent India. Although he had briefly joined the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party in 1951, he returned to the Congress. He is remembered for his important role in food distribution and agricultural policy. He was not associated with the Muslim League, CPI, or the Socialist Party.
questions.solution_hindi: रफी अहमद किदवई भारतीय राष्ट्रीय काँग्रेस (विकल्प B) से संबंधित थे। वे नेहरू के निकट सहयोगी थे और स्वतंत्र भारत में खाद्य एवं कृषि मंत्री रहे।

questions.text: नीति आयोग में दर्ज 'NITI' (नीति) शब्द का सही विस्तृत रूप चुनिए।
questions.text_english: Choose the correct full form of 'NITI' of NITI Aayog.
questions.solution: The correct full form of NITI in NITI Aayog is 'National Institution for Transforming India' (option D). NITI Aayog was established in January 2015 to replace the Planning Commission. It serves as the Government of India's premier policy think tank and promotes cooperative federalism. Options A, B, and C are all incorrect expansions of the acronym and do not correspond to the actual name of the institution.
questions.solution_hindi: NITI आयोग में NITI का पूर्ण रूप 'नेशनल इंस्टीट्यूशन फॉर ट्रांसफॉर्मिंग इंडिया' (विकल्प D) है। इसे जनवरी 2015 में योजना आयोग के स्थान पर स्थापित किया गया था।

questions.text: दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना निम्नलिखित में से किस पर केंद्रित थी ?
questions.text_english: The focus of the Second Five Year Plan was :
questions.solution: The Second Five Year Plan (1956–61) focused on Heavy Industries (option C). It was based on the Mahalanobis Model and emphasised the development of heavy and capital goods industries as the foundation for rapid industrialisation. The plan led to the establishment of steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela. The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) had focused on agriculture and rehabilitation. Atomic energy and small scale industries were not the primary focus of the Second Plan.
questions.solution_hindi: दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-61) भारी उद्योगों (विकल्प C) पर केंद्रित थी। यह महालनोबिस मॉडल पर आधारित थी और इसके अंतर्गत भिलाई, दुर्गापुर और राउरकेला में इस्पात संयंत्र स्थापित किए गए।

questions.text: यूरोपीय संघ की अर्थव्यवस्था किस प्रकार संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका की अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए एक खतरा बन सकती है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How can the economy of the European Union pose a threat to the US economy ? Explain.

key_points: EU has the world's largest economy in terms of GDP and its own currency, the Euro, which rivals the US dollar.
EU is a major trading bloc that competes with the US in global markets for goods, services, and technology.
EU's economic policies and trade agreements challenge US dominance in international trade and financial institutions.

questions.solution: The European Union poses an economic threat to the United States because the EU collectively has one of the largest economies in the world, with a GDP that rivals or surpasses that of the US. The Euro, the EU's common currency, competes with the US dollar as the global reserve currency, reducing American financial dominance. The EU also functions as a powerful unified trading bloc, competing with the US in global markets for goods, services, and technology. Additionally, EU trade agreements with third countries challenge American trade interests. The EU's economic clout enables it to set global standards in areas like digital regulation and environmental policy, often affecting US businesses.
questions.solution_hindi: यूरोपीय संघ की अर्थव्यवस्था कई कारणों से अमेरिका के लिए खतरा बन सकती है। यूरो (EU की मुद्रा) अमेरिकी डॉलर को वैश्विक आरक्षित मुद्रा के रूप में चुनौती देती है। EU का संयुक्त GDP अमेरिका के समकक्ष है। EU एक बड़े व्यापार गुट के रूप में वैश्विक बाजारों में अमेरिका से प्रतिस्पर्धा करता है।
questions.topic: European Union as an Economic Power

questions.text: किन्हीं चार वैश्विक साझी सम्पदाओं के नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Name any four Global Commons.

key_points: Earth's atmosphere / air space beyond national jurisdiction
Antarctica
High seas (international waters beyond national jurisdiction)
Outer space

questions.solution: The four main Global Commons are: (1) The Earth's atmosphere, which includes the air space beyond national jurisdiction that all nations share; (2) Antarctica, the continent governed collectively through the Antarctic Treaty System; (3) The High Seas, that is, international waters beyond any country's Exclusive Economic Zone; and (4) Outer Space, the region beyond Earth's atmosphere that no single nation can claim sovereign ownership over. These areas are considered the common heritage of humanity and are managed through international agreements.
questions.solution_hindi: चार प्रमुख वैश्विक साझी सम्पदाएं हैं: (1) पृथ्वी का वायुमंडल (राष्ट्रीय क्षेत्राधिकार से परे), (2) अंटार्कटिका, (3) उच्च समुद्र (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय जल क्षेत्र), और (4) बाह्य अंतरिक्ष। ये क्षेत्र किसी एक देश के स्वामित्व में नहीं हैं और संपूर्ण मानवता की साझी विरासत हैं।

questions.text: "वैश्विक राजनीति के लिए 'जल' एक प्रासंगिक महत्त्वपूर्ण संसाधन है।" एक उदाहरण की सहायता से कथन को सिद्ध कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Water is a crucial resource that is relevant to global politics." Justify the statement with the help of one example.

key_points: Freshwater scarcity is predicted to become a major cause of inter-state conflict in the coming decades.
Example: Disputes over river water sharing between riparian countries, such as India–Bangladesh dispute over Ganga waters or the Nile dispute among African nations.

questions.solution: Water is indeed a crucial resource in global politics because freshwater is unevenly distributed across the world and is increasingly scarce. Many nations share the same rivers or aquifers, creating potential for conflict. For example, the dispute over the waters of the river Nile between Ethiopia, Sudan, and Egypt is a major geopolitical issue. Ethiopia's construction of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam has threatened Egypt's share of Nile waters, bringing the two nations close to conflict. This shows how water, as a shared but limited resource, can become a central issue in global politics and international relations.
questions.solution_hindi: जल वैश्विक राजनीति में अत्यंत महत्त्वपूर्ण संसाधन है क्योंकि मीठे पानी का असमान वितरण है। उदाहरण के लिए, नील नदी के जल पर इथियोपिया, सूडान और मिस्र के बीच विवाद एक बड़ा भू-राजनीतिक मुद्दा है। इसी प्रकार भारत-बांग्लादेश के बीच गंगा जल बंटवारे का विवाद है जो दर्शाता है कि जल अंतर्राष्ट्रीय राजनीति में कैसे महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।

questions.text: कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया ने 1951 में हिंसक क्रान्ति के रास्ते को क्यों छोड़ा ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Why did the Communist Party of India abandon the path of violent revolution in 1951 ? Explain.

key_points: The Telangana armed uprising (1946–51) failed and was suppressed by the government.
CPI decided to participate in the 1952 general elections as a legitimate political party and contest power through democratic means.

questions.solution: The Communist Party of India (CPI) abandoned the path of violent revolution in 1951 primarily because the Telangana armed uprising, which it had led since 1946, was decisively suppressed by the Indian government and military forces. The failure of this peasant-based armed struggle demonstrated that violent revolution was not a viable strategy in democratic India. The CPI then made a pragmatic decision to participate in the first general elections of 1952, choosing to work within the constitutional framework to achieve its political goals. This shift to parliamentary democracy proved successful, as the CPI emerged as the main opposition party after the 1952 elections.
questions.solution_hindi: कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया ने 1951 में हिंसक क्रान्ति का मार्ग छोड़ा क्योंकि 1946 से चल रहा तेलंगाना सशस्त्र संघर्ष भारत सरकार द्वारा दबा दिया गया था। हिंसक क्रान्ति विफल होने पर पार्टी ने 1952 के पहले आम चुनावों में भाग लेने का निर्णय किया और संसदीय लोकतंत्र के मार्ग पर चलने लगी।

questions.text: एशियाई और एफ्रो-एशियाई एकता के लिए भारत द्वारा उठाए गए किन्हीं दो कदमों को उजागर कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two steps taken by India for Asian and Afro-Asian Unity.

key_points: India organised the Asian Relations Conference in New Delhi in 1947, bringing together Asian nations to promote regional solidarity.
India played a key role in the Bandung Conference (1955) in Indonesia, which led to the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement and promoted Afro-Asian unity.

questions.solution: India took two major steps for Asian and Afro-Asian unity. First, India hosted the Asian Relations Conference in New Delhi in 1947, even before its formal independence, bringing together representatives from across Asia to foster solidarity and discuss common concerns. Second, India was a leading participant in the Bandung Conference held in Indonesia in 1955, which brought together 29 Asian and African nations to promote Afro-Asian solidarity, oppose colonialism and imperialism, and lay the groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement. Nehru's active diplomacy was central to both these initiatives.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत ने एशियाई और एफ्रो-एशियाई एकता के लिए दो प्रमुख कदम उठाए। पहला, 1947 में नई दिल्ली में एशियाई संबंध सम्मेलन का आयोजन किया। दूसरा, 1955 में इंडोनेशिया के बांडुंग सम्मेलन में सक्रिय भागीदारी की जिसने गुट-निरपेक्ष आंदोलन की नींव रखी।

questions.text: 1989 से 1999 के बीच भारतीय राजनीति की किन्हीं दो प्रमुख समस्याओं का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Analyse any two major problems of Indian politics from 1989 to 1999.

key_points: Political instability due to fragile coalition governments — between 1989 and 1999 India had several short-lived governments.
Rise of identity politics and communal tensions, exemplified by the Mandal Commission controversy and the Babri Masjid demolition in 1992, which deepened social and religious divisions.

questions.solution: The period from 1989 to 1999 was marked by two major problems in Indian politics. First, there was severe political instability due to the era of coalition governments. The Congress Party lost its dominant position and no single party could win a majority, resulting in a succession of fragile governments. India had five Prime Ministers in this period alone, reflecting the instability. Second, this era witnessed a sharp intensification of identity politics based on caste and religion. The implementation of the Mandal Commission report on OBC reservations triggered widespread protests, and the demolition of the Babri Masjid in 1992 unleashed communal violence that deepened Hindu–Muslim divisions across the country.
questions.solution_hindi: 1989 से 1999 के बीच भारतीय राजनीति की दो प्रमुख समस्याएं थीं। पहली, राजनीतिक अस्थिरता — इस दशक में पाँच प्रधानमंत्री बदले और कोई भी एकल दल स्पष्ट बहुमत नहीं पा सका। दूसरी, जातीय और धार्मिक पहचान की राजनीति का उभार — मंडल आयोग विवाद तथा 1992 में बाबरी मस्जिद विध्वंस से सांप्रदायिक तनाव बढ़ा।

questions.text: स्वतंत्रता के बाद से भारत और चीन के बीच आपसी सम्बन्धों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Analyse the relations between India and China since independence.

key_points: Early friendship: India recognised communist China and the two countries signed the Panchsheel agreement in 1954.
Strain: China's annexation of Tibet (1950) removed a historical buffer between the two countries.
1962 War: Boundary dispute led to China's invasion in 1962, which India lost, severely damaging bilateral trust.
Gradual normalisation: From the 1970s onwards, relations slowly improved with high-level visits and trade growth.
Contemporary challenges: Border disputes (Aksai Chin and Arunachal Pradesh) persist alongside growing economic ties.

questions.solution:
India–China relations since independence have passed through several distinct phases. In the early years, the relationship was warm and cooperative. India was one of the first countries to recognise the People's Republic of China in 1950, and in 1954 the two nations jointly signed the Panchsheel agreement, declaring five principles of peaceful coexistence. The popular slogan 'Hindi-Chini bhai bhai' captured this spirit of friendship.

However, relations quickly deteriorated when China annexed Tibet in 1950, eliminating the traditional buffer between the two countries. A serious boundary dispute soon emerged over the Aksai Chin region in the west and the McMahon Line in the east. In 1959, China objected to India granting political asylum to the Dalai Lama, who had fled Tibet. These tensions culminated in China's military invasion in 1962, in which India suffered a humiliating defeat. This war left a deep wound in bilateral relations that persisted for decades.

Slow normalisation began in the 1970s and 1980s. Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi visited China in 1988, marking a turning point. Trade relations expanded rapidly after India's economic liberalisation in 1991. Today India and China are each other's major trading partners. However, unresolved border disputes, China's growing military presence in the Indian Ocean, and its close ties with Pakistan continue to strain the relationship.
questions.solution_hindi: स्वतंत्रता के बाद भारत-चीन संबंध कई चरणों से गुज़रे। प्रारंभ में संबंध मैत्रीपूर्ण थे — भारत ने 1950 में चीन की कम्युनिस्ट सरकार को मान्यता दी और 1954 में पंचशील समझौते पर हस्ताक्षर किए। लेकिन तिब्बत पर चीन के कब्जे, सीमा विवाद और 1959 में दलाई लामा को भारत द्वारा शरण देने से संबंध बिगड़े। 1962 के युद्ध में भारत की हार ने संबंधों को गहरा आघात पहुंचाया। 1988 में राजीव गांधी की चीन यात्रा से धीरे-धीरे संबंध सामान्य हुए।

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Explain the reasons for ethnic conflict in Sri Lanka and its impact on India.

key_points: Reasons: Sinhala-Tamil rivalry, Sinhala-only language policy of 1956, discrimination against Tamils in government jobs and education.
Rise of LTTE and armed separatist movement for a Tamil homeland (Eelam).
Impact on India: Large influx of Tamil refugees into Tamil Nadu, domestic political pressure on the Indian government.
India's military intervention: India sent IPKF (Indian Peace Keeping Force) in 1987 which suffered significant casualties.

sub_questions.solution:
Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict arose primarily from the deep-rooted rivalry between the Sinhalese majority and the Tamil minority. After independence in 1948, the Sinhalese-dominated government passed the Sinhala-only Act in 1956, making Sinhala the sole official language and effectively sidelining Tamil speakers. Tamils also faced systematic discrimination in government employment and university admissions. These grievances fuelled Tamil militancy, leading to the rise of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), which demanded a separate Tamil homeland called Eelam in northern and eastern Sri Lanka. By the 1980s, this had become a full-scale civil war.

The conflict had a profound impact on India. Geographically close to Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka's civil war caused hundreds of thousands of Tamil refugees to flee across the Palk Strait into India, creating a severe humanitarian crisis. Politically, Tamil groups in India sympathised with Sri Lankan Tamils, creating immense pressure on the Indian government to intervene. India initially tried diplomatic means and eventually signed the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord in 1987, sending the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) to Sri Lanka. The IPKF mission proved costly and controversial, leading to significant Indian military casualties. The conflict also resulted in the assassination of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 by an LTTE suicide bomber.

sub_questions.text: (ख) भारत और नेपाल के बीच अच्छे सम्बन्धों के किन्हीं चार कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Explain any four reasons for good relations between Nepal and India.

key_points: Geographical proximity and open border allowing free movement of people.
Shared cultural, religious, and linguistic ties.
Economic interdependence: Nepal depends heavily on India for trade and transit.
Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1950) providing special privileges to citizens of both countries.

sub_questions.solution: India and Nepal share a historically deep and friendly relationship based on four key reasons. First, the two countries share an open border that allows the free movement of people, facilitating family ties, trade, and cultural exchange. Nepali citizens can work and live in India and vice versa under special provisions. Second, India and Nepal share deep cultural, religious, and linguistic bonds. Hinduism, Buddhism, and many traditions are common to both nations, and the people of the Terai region of Nepal share close ethnic ties with people of the Indo-Gangetic plains. Third, there is strong economic interdependence, as Nepal is a landlocked country that depends almost entirely on India for access to the sea, trade routes, and the import of essential goods like fuel and medicines. Fourth, the Treaty of Peace and Friendship signed in 1950 provides citizens of both countries special rights and privileges in each other's territory, forming the legal foundation of their close relationship.

questions.text: उदाहरणों की सहायता से दर्शाइए कि विचारों, पूँजी, वस्तुओं और लोगों का प्रवाह वैश्वीकरण के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।
questions.text_english: Show with the help of examples that flows of ideas, capital, commodities and people are instrumental for globalisation.

key_points: Flow of ideas: Internet and social media spread knowledge and cultural values across borders.
Flow of capital: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) by multinational corporations connects economies.
Flow of commodities: International trade in goods like electronics, clothing and food integrates markets.
Flow of people: Migration of workers, students and professionals creates global labour markets.

questions.solution:
Globalisation is fundamentally driven by four types of flows, each of which can be illustrated with concrete examples. The flow of ideas means that knowledge, culture, and values cross national borders rapidly. For example, the internet and social media platforms allow people worldwide to share information, scientific discoveries, and cultural trends instantaneously. A software idea developed in Silicon Valley can be refined by engineers in Bengaluru and used by consumers in Europe within hours.

The flow of capital refers to the movement of money across borders for investment. Multinational corporations like Samsung or Apple invest billions of dollars in countries like India and Vietnam to set up manufacturing units, creating employment and connecting local economies to global supply chains. This FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) is a central pillar of globalisation.

The flow of commodities means the international trade in goods. A single smartphone contains components made in dozens of countries — chips from Taiwan, screens from South Korea, and assembled in China for sale globally. This complex interdependence in trade illustrates commodity flows.

Finally, the flow of people means the migration of workers, professionals, and students across borders. Indian IT professionals working in the United States, or Nepali workers employed in Gulf countries, are examples of how human movement integrates economies and cultures globally.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण के लिए चार प्रकार के प्रवाह महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं। विचारों का प्रवाह: इंटरनेट के माध्यम से ज्ञान और संस्कृति विश्वभर में फैलती है। पूँजी का प्रवाह: बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियों द्वारा विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश (FDI)। वस्तुओं का प्रवाह: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार में विभिन्न देशों के उत्पाद शामिल हैं। लोगों का प्रवाह: कुशल श्रमिकों और पेशेवरों का एक देश से दूसरे देश जाना।

(a) Describe any four consequences of the partition of British India.
OR

sub_questions.text: (क) ब्रिटिश इंडिया के विभाजन के किन्हीं चार परिणामों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Describe any four consequences of the partition of British India.

key_points: Massive displacement of population — approximately 1.5 crore people crossed borders between India and Pakistan.
Widespread communal violence, riots, and massacres, resulting in lakhs of deaths.
Refugee crisis placing enormous administrative and economic strain on the new governments.
Division of the military, civil services, and assets between India and Pakistan.

sub_questions.solution: The partition of British India in 1947 had four major consequences. First, it triggered the largest mass migration in human history. Approximately one and a half crore people — Hindus and Sikhs moving to India, Muslims moving to Pakistan — crossed borders in both directions within weeks, creating enormous humanitarian upheaval. Second, the partition was accompanied by horrific communal violence. Riots, massacres, and atrocities occurred on an unprecedented scale in Punjab and Bengal, with estimates of deaths ranging from two to five lakh people. Women were particularly targeted through abduction and violence. Third, the refugee crisis placed an enormous burden on the newly independent governments of India and Pakistan. Millions of uprooted people needed shelter, food, employment, and rehabilitation. Fourth, the partition required the complex division of the colonial administration, military, financial assets, railway networks, and civil services between the two new nations, creating lasting institutional challenges and disputes over resources such as river waters.

sub_questions.text: (ख) ब्रिटिश इंडिया के विभाजन की प्रक्रिया की किन्हीं चार समस्याओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Describe any four problems of the process of partition of British India.

key_points: Demarcation of boundaries was rushed and contested, especially the Radcliffe Line in Punjab and Bengal.
Problem of mixed populations in regions where Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs lived together.
Problem of integrating princely states into the two new nations.
Division of financial assets and military resources was contentious and complex.

sub_questions.solution: The process of partition of British India in 1947 was fraught with four major problems. First, the demarcation of the boundary between India and Pakistan was carried out hastily by the Boundary Commission under Sir Cyril Radcliffe, who had never visited India before. The resulting Radcliffe Line was announced only after independence, leaving communities uncertain and contributing to panic-driven migration and violence. Second, the problem of mixed populations was acute in Punjab and Bengal, where Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs were interspersed across the same villages and cities. No line could cleanly separate them, making displacement inevitable. Third, the question of the princely states posed a serious challenge. The nearly 565 princely states had to decide whether to join India or Pakistan, and the process of their accession was complicated, contested, and in some cases (like Hyderabad and Kashmir) led to military conflict. Fourth, dividing the financial reserves, military assets, administrative records, and infrastructure of a unified colonial state between two entirely new countries was an extraordinarily complex logistical challenge.

questions.text: 1975 में लगाए गए आपातकाल के विरोध को नियंत्रित करने के लिए सरकार द्वारा उठाए गए किन्हीं चार कदमों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any four steps taken by the government to control the opposition to Emergency imposed in 1975.

key_points: Suspension of Fundamental Rights including the right to move courts for their enforcement.
Arrest and imprisonment of opposition leaders including Jayaprakash Narayan, Morarji Desai, and others.
Imposition of press censorship — newspapers were prohibited from publishing anything critical of the government.
Banning of organisations such as the RSS, Jamaat-e-Islami, and other groups perceived as threats.

questions.solution: When the Emergency was declared on 25 June 1975, the Indira Gandhi government took four major steps to suppress opposition. First, Fundamental Rights were suspended, including the right to constitutional remedies, which meant citizens could not approach courts to challenge their detention. The right to life and personal liberty (Article 21) was effectively curtailed. Second, the government arrested thousands of opposition leaders, activists, and journalists under preventive detention laws. Prominent leaders like Jayaprakash Narayan, Morarji Desai, Atal Bihari Vajpayee, and L.K. Advani were jailed without trial. Third, strict press censorship was imposed. Newspapers were required to submit their content to government censors before publication, preventing any critical reporting. Some newspapers left their editorial columns blank in silent protest. Fourth, several political and social organisations were banned. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), Jamaat-e-Islami, and the Ananda Marga were among those prohibited. These measures together effectively silenced all organised opposition to the Emergency.
questions.solution_hindi: 1975 के आपातकाल के दौरान सरकार ने विरोध को दबाने के लिए चार प्रमुख कदम उठाए। पहला, मूल अधिकारों को निलंबित किया गया। दूसरा, जयप्रकाश नारायण, मोरारजी देसाई सहित विपक्षी नेताओं को बिना मुकदमे के जेल में डाला गया। तीसरा, प्रेस पर कड़ी सेंसरशिप लगाई गई। चौथा, RSS, जमात-ए-इस्लामी जैसे संगठनों पर प्रतिबंध लगाया गया।

निम्नलिखित अवतरण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इस पर आधारित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए:

"चीनी क्रान्ति के बाद भारत, चीन की कम्युनिस्ट सरकार को मान्यता देने वाले पहले देशों में से एक था। इस पड़ोसी देश को लेकर नेहरू के हृदय में गहरे भाव थे और उन्होंने अन्तर्राष्ट्रीय फलक पर इस नई सरकार की मदद की। शान्तिपूर्ण सहअस्तित्व की घोषणा पर 1954 में भारत के प्रधानमंत्री और चीन के प्रमुख ने संयुक्त रूप से हस्ताक्षर किए। लेकिन दो घटनाओं से इस रिश्ते में खटास आ गई। चीन ने तिब्बत पर कब्जा कर लिया और दोनों देशों के बीच के ऐतिहासिक मध्यवर्ती राज्य को समाप्त कर दिया। इससे पहले भारत और चीन के बीच एक सीमा विवाद भी उठ खड़ा हुआ था।"
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on it:

"After the Chinese revolution, India was one of the first countries to recognise the communist government. Nehru felt strongly for this neighbour and helped the new government in international fora. A joint enunciation of peaceful coexistence was signed by Indian Prime Minister and the Chinese premier in 1954. But two developments strained this relationship. China annexed Tibet and removed a historical buffer between the two countries. A little earlier, a boundary dispute had surfaced between India and China."

sub_questions.text_english: In which year was Tibet annexed by China ?
sub_questions.solution: China annexed Tibet in 1950 (option B). In October 1950, the People's Liberation Army of China entered Tibet and militarily incorporated it into the People's Republic of China. This removed the traditional buffer state between India and China and was a key development that contributed to the eventual deterioration of Sino-Indian relations.

sub_questions.text: भारत में राजनीतिक शरण प्राप्त करने वाले तिब्बत के आध्यात्मिक नेता का नाम चुनिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Choose the name of the Tibetan spiritual leader who had obtained political asylum in India.
sub_questions.solution: The Dalai Lama (option A) is the Tibetan spiritual leader who obtained political asylum in India. In 1959, following a failed uprising against Chinese rule in Tibet, the 14th Dalai Lama fled to India and was granted asylum by the Indian government. He established the Tibetan government-in-exile in Dharamsala, Himachal Pradesh. This decision angered China and further strained Indo-China relations.

sub_questions.text: 1954 में भारत और चीन ने निम्नलिखित में से किस पर संयुक्त रूप से हस्ताक्षर किए थे ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following was jointly signed by India and China in 1954 ?
sub_questions.solution: India and China jointly signed the Panchsheel agreement (option B) in 1954. Panchsheel, also known as the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, was signed between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai. The five principles included mutual respect for sovereignty, mutual non-aggression, non-interference in internal affairs, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. It was a foundational document in post-war Asian diplomacy.

options.D: भारत के सं.रा. अमेरिका के साथ अच्छे संबंध

sub_questions.solution: The primary stated reason for China's invasion of India in 1962 was the boundary dispute (option A). China and India disagreed over the location of the border in two regions — the Aksai Chin area in the west (Ladakh) and the area south of the McMahon Line in the east (present-day Arunachal Pradesh). India's 'Forward Policy' of establishing military posts near the disputed border further inflamed tensions, and China launched a massive military offensive in October 1962, quickly advancing deep into Indian territory before declaring a ceasefire.

sub_questions.text: (क) 'शॉक थेरेपी' को एक सत्तावादी समाजवादी व्यवस्था से लोकतांत्रिक पूँजीवादी व्यवस्था में संक्रमण की कष्टप्रद प्रक्रिया क्यों माना जाता है ? कोई तीन कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Why is 'Shock Therapy' considered a painful process of transition from an authoritarian socialist system to a democratic capitalist system ? Explain any three reasons.

key_points: Sudden dismantling of state-run industries led to massive unemployment and economic collapse.
Rapid privatisation caused the ruble to lose its value and wiped out people's savings, creating widespread poverty.
Withdrawal of state subsidies on food, housing, and essential services caused acute hardship for ordinary citizens.

sub_questions.solution:
Shock Therapy is considered a painful process of transition for three major reasons. First, the sudden and rapid dismantling of the state-run command economy led to the collapse of industries and the closure of thousands of factories. Millions of workers lost their jobs almost overnight, creating mass unemployment and social instability on an unprecedented scale. Countries like Russia and other former Soviet republics saw their GDP decline sharply in the early 1990s.

Second, the process of rapid privatisation of state assets was deeply flawed. State enterprises were sold off hastily, often at throwaway prices, allowing a small group of politically connected individuals to acquire enormous wealth. This created a class of powerful 'oligarchs' while ordinary citizens saw the value of the ruble collapse and their life savings wiped out. Hyperinflation eroded purchasing power and pushed large sections of the population into poverty.

Third, the withdrawal of state subsidies on food, housing, healthcare, and education — which socialist states had provided — was sudden and comprehensive. Ordinary people who had depended on these subsidies for generations found themselves unable to afford basic necessities. The social safety net that the state had provided simply disappeared, leading to a dramatic decline in living standards, health outcomes, and life expectancy in countries undergoing Shock Therapy.

sub_questions.text: (ख) सोवियत संघ के विघटन के किन्हीं चार कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Explain any four reasons for the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Economic stagnation: Soviet economy was unable to match Western consumer goods or technology.
Rise of nationalism among constituent republics demanding independence.
Gorbachev's reforms (Glasnost and Perestroika) weakened central control without creating viable alternatives.
The arms race and Cold War drained Soviet resources, making economic sustainability impossible.

sub_questions.solution:
The disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991 resulted from four interconnected causes. First, the Soviet economy was experiencing deep structural stagnation by the 1980s. The command economy was inefficient, technologically backward compared to the West, and unable to meet the consumer needs of its citizens. The gap between Soviet living standards and those in Western Europe became increasingly visible and demoralising.

Second, the arms race with the United States during the Cold War imposed a crushing financial burden on the Soviet economy. The USSR spent a disproportionately large share of its national income on defence and space programmes, starving the civilian economy of resources and contributing to long-term decline.

Third, Mikhail Gorbachev's reform programmes of Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring) had unintended consequences. While intended to revitalise the Soviet system, they loosened central control, enabled free expression of discontent, and emboldened nationalist movements. Political liberalisation without economic improvement created a volatile situation.

Fourth, rising nationalist sentiments among the fifteen Soviet republics became an irresistible force. Baltic states like Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania demanded independence, and their example inspired others. By 1991, the centrifugal forces of nationalism had become too powerful for the Soviet centre to contain, and the union formally dissolved in December 1991.

questions.text: (क) सुरक्षा की अपारम्परिक धारणा को मानव सुरक्षा की धारणा के रूप में विश्लेषित कीजिए।

sub_questions.text: (क) सुरक्षा की अपारम्परिक धारणा को मानव सुरक्षा की धारणा के रूप में विश्लेषित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Analyse the non-traditional notion of security as a notion of human security.

key_points: Non-traditional security shifts focus from the state to the individual as the referent object of security.
Human security encompasses freedom from fear (violence, war, terrorism) and freedom from want (poverty, disease, hunger).
Threats include global terrorism, climate change, pandemics, poverty, and human rights violations.
International cooperation and multilateral institutions are essential to address these threats.
UNDP's 1994 Human Development Report popularised the concept of human security.

sub_questions.solution:
The non-traditional notion of security represents a fundamental shift in how we understand what needs to be protected, from whom, and by what means. Traditional security focused on protecting the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the state from external military threats. The non-traditional or human security paradigm, by contrast, places the individual human being — not the state — at the centre of security concerns.

The concept of human security was elaborated by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in its 1994 Human Development Report. It identified two core components: freedom from fear and freedom from want. Freedom from fear means protecting individuals from violence — whether from war, terrorism, genocide, or organised crime. Freedom from want means protecting people from deprivation — including poverty, hunger, disease, and lack of access to basic services like healthcare and education.

Non-traditional security threats are diverse and interconnected. They include global terrorism, which can strike anywhere and targets civilians directly; climate change and environmental degradation, which threaten food and water security; pandemics such as HIV/AIDS or COVID-19, which kill millions and destabilise economies; and global poverty and inequality, which deny billions of people dignity and opportunity.

Addressing these threats requires international cooperation, multilateral institutions, and a commitment to human rights. No single state can address global terrorism, climate change, or pandemics alone. The non-traditional security framework thus demands shared responsibility among states and a focus on the well-being of all people, not merely the defence of state borders.

sub_questions.text: (ख) "भारत ने पिछले दो दशकों में सुरक्षा की अपारम्परिक धारणा को प्राथमिकता दी है।" उदाहरणों के साथ कथन का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) "India has given priority to non-traditional security in the last two decades." Analyse the statement with examples.

key_points: India's active role in disaster relief operations, e.g. tsunami relief in 2004.
Counter-terrorism cooperation at global level and participation in UN peacekeeping missions.
Climate change commitments: India's solar energy expansion and Paris Agreement participation.
Health security: India's role as 'pharmacy of the world' and COVID-19 vaccine diplomacy.
Food security initiatives and poverty alleviation programmes addressing human development.

sub_questions.solution:
The statement that India has given priority to non-traditional security in the last two decades is well supported by evidence across several domains. Non-traditional security focuses on human welfare, environmental safety, and cooperative responses to transnational threats rather than on military defence alone.

First, India has been a major contributor to United Nations Peacekeeping Operations, deploying thousands of troops to conflict zones in Africa, the Middle East, and Asia. This reflects India's commitment to global peace and human security beyond its own borders. Second, in the area of disaster relief, India launched Operation Sea Waves in 2004 after the Indian Ocean tsunami, providing immediate humanitarian assistance to Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Indonesia, demonstrating its capacity and willingness to address human emergencies regionally.

Third, on climate change, India signed the Paris Agreement in 2016 and has made ambitious commitments to expand renewable energy. India's International Solar Alliance initiative seeks to mobilise solar energy across developing countries, addressing both energy poverty and environmental security. Fourth, in health security, India has earned recognition as the 'pharmacy of the world' by supplying affordable generic medicines globally. During the COVID-19 pandemic, India's Vaccine Maitri programme supplied millions of doses to developing countries, prioritising global human security. These examples demonstrate that India's security strategy in the 21st century extends well beyond conventional military defence to embrace the full range of human security concerns.

sub_questions.text: (क) पंजाब से जुड़ी किन्हीं तीन प्रमुख घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए जिनसे वहाँ के लोगों में असन्तोष और हिंसा का संचार हुआ।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Describe any three major developments witnessed by Punjab that led to dissatisfaction and violence.

key_points: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) demanding greater autonomy for Punjab and Sikh religious rights.
Operation Blue Star (June 1984) — the Indian Army's storming of the Golden Temple in Amritsar to flush out militants, which deeply hurt Sikh sentiments.
The assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi (October 1984) by her Sikh bodyguards and the subsequent anti-Sikh riots in Delhi and other cities.

sub_questions.solution:
Three major developments in Punjab that fuelled dissatisfaction and violence are as follows. The first was the Anandpur Sahib Resolution of 1973, passed by the Shiromani Akali Dal. This resolution demanded greater political and religious autonomy for Punjab, control over river waters, and resolution of the Chandigarh capital dispute. The government's failure to address these demands created deep political discontent among Sikhs and provided fertile ground for the rise of militant groups.

The second was Operation Blue Star in June 1984. Militant leader Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale and his armed followers had taken sanctuary inside the sacred Golden Temple complex in Amritsar. The Indian Army was ordered to flush them out, and the military operation resulted in significant casualties and damage to the holy shrine. This deeply wounded Sikh religious sentiments across India and the world, and is widely considered the event that radicalised an entire generation and dramatically intensified violence in Punjab.

The third was the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in October 1984 by two of her Sikh bodyguards in retaliation for Operation Blue Star. This triggered organised anti-Sikh riots in Delhi and several other cities, in which thousands of Sikhs were killed. These riots deepened the alienation of the Sikh community from the Indian state and prolonged the cycle of violence and counter-violence in Punjab through the rest of the 1980s.

sub_questions.text: (ख) ऐसे किन्हीं तीन उपायों का वर्णन कीजिए जो संघीय सरकार द्वारा क्षेत्रीय आन्दोलनों और माँगों को हल करने के लिए अपनाए जा सकते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Describe any three measures that can be taken by the Union government to address the regional movements and demands.

key_points: Negotiation and dialogue with regional groups to address legitimate grievances peacefully.
Creation of new states or reorganisation of boundaries to meet linguistic/cultural demands.
Decentralisation of power and greater financial autonomy to states through fiscal federalism.

sub_questions.solution:
The Union government can adopt three broad categories of measures to address regional movements and demands. The first is political dialogue and negotiation. When regional movements arise from genuine economic, cultural, or political grievances, the government can engage in direct talks with representatives of the movement to find mutually acceptable solutions. The signing of accords — such as the Rajiv Gandhi–Longowal Accord for Punjab in 1985 or the Assam Accord of 1985 — demonstrates that dialogue can be an effective instrument for de-escalating conflicts and addressing core demands.

The second measure is administrative reorganisation, including the creation of new states or granting greater autonomy within the existing framework. India has a precedent of responding to regional demands through state reorganisation. The creation of states like Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Uttarakhand in 2000 addressed the aspirations of distinct regional communities. Where cultural and linguistic identities are strong, recognising them through administrative arrangements can defuse separatist tendencies.

The third measure is economic development and fiscal decentralisation. Many regional movements draw their strength from perceived economic neglect or exploitation. The Union government can address this by ensuring equitable distribution of central funds, prioritising development projects in backward regions, and granting states greater fiscal autonomy. Empowering Panchayati Raj institutions and local bodies further ensures that development reaches the grassroots level, reducing the appeal of regional agitations.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) State any four major political happenings of the decade of the nineties which had a widespread impact.

key_points: Demolition of Babri Masjid (December 1992) and subsequent communal riots.
Implementation of Mandal Commission recommendations (1990) leading to OBC reservations and widespread protests.
Economic liberalisation (1991) — India's New Economic Policy opening the economy to private and foreign investment.
Rise of coalition politics and emergence of regional parties as power brokers at the national level.

The decade of the 1990s was politically tumultuous in India, and four major happenings of that decade had widespread and lasting impact. The first was the implementation of the Mandal Commission's recommendations in 1990 by the V.P. Singh government, reserving 27% of central government jobs for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). This triggered massive protests by upper-caste youth, including self-immolation attempts, and permanently altered the landscape of identity-based politics. Caste became a central axis of electoral mobilisation.

The second was the demolition of the Babri Masjid at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992 by a crowd of Hindu activists. This act of communal violence shattered the secular political consensus and triggered riots across India in which thousands of people died. The event polarised Hindu and Muslim communities deeply and gave a decisive boost to the rise of the Bharatiya Janata Party as the principal challenger to Congress.

The third was the New Economic Policy introduced by Finance Minister Manmohan Singh in 1991 under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao. India dismantled the Licence Raj, devalued the rupee, reduced import tariffs, and opened the economy to foreign investment. This fundamentally transformed India's economic trajectory and integrated it into the global economy. The fourth was the rise of coalition politics, as no single party won a clear majority throughout the decade. Regional parties like the SP, BSP, TDP, and DMK became kingmakers, fundamentally shifting the balance of power from the national to the regional level in Indian democracy.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Describe any four issues on which a broad agreement has emerged among most of the political parties in India.

key_points: Commitment to liberal economic policies and economic reforms (new economic policy framework).
Acceptance of the political and social claims of the backward castes (OBC reservations).
Commitment to the policy of accommodation of regional demands within the federal framework.
Acceptance of democratic decentralisation through Panchayati Raj institutions.

sub_questions.solution:
In contemporary Indian politics, despite fierce electoral competition, a broad consensus has emerged among most political parties on four key issues. The first is acceptance of the new economic policy framework. While parties may differ on emphasis, there is general agreement across the political spectrum — from the BJP and Congress to regional parties — that economic liberalisation, privatisation, and integration into the global economy are broadly beneficial and should continue. No major party advocates a return to a closed, state-controlled economy.

The second area of consensus is the acceptance of social justice claims, particularly those of the Other Backward Classes (OBCs). After the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations and the political mobilisation it unleashed, virtually all parties now accept the principle of OBC reservations and compete actively for the support of backward class communities. The politics of social justice has become mainstream across party lines.

The third area is accommodation of regional aspirations within the framework of Indian federalism. Most parties — both national and regional — accept that India's diversity demands a flexible federal structure that can accommodate the linguistic, cultural, and economic aspirations of different regions. The creation of new states and the devolution of powers are broadly accepted tools for managing regional demands.

The fourth area is commitment to democratic decentralisation through Panchayati Raj institutions. Following the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments of 1992, most parties accept that empowering local governments — gram panchayats, panchayat samitis, and urban local bodies — is essential for deepening democracy and delivering development at the grassroots level.
